name: Camp Nou
historyClues: Opened in 1957 and expanded several times during the 20th century.
Its capacity once exceeded 120,000 before all-seater regulations.
Hosted European finals and countless El Clásicos.
Located in the Les Corts area of Barcelona.

name: Santiago Bernabéu
historyClues: Opened in 1947 and undergoing major modern renovations in the 2020s.
Named after a former club president.
Hosted multiple European Cup finals.
Situated on Paseo de la Castellana.

name: Old Trafford
historyClues: Opened in 1910 and rebuilt after heavy damage in World War II.
Nicknamed the Theatre of Dreams.
Record domestic attendances before all-seater rules.
Located in Greater Manchester, in Old Trafford.

name: Anfield
historyClues: Opened in 1884 and became Liverpool's home in 1892.
The Kop is one of the most famous stands in world football.
Known for its electric European nights.
Expanded Main Stand in the mid-2010s.

name: Allianz Arena
historyClues: Opened in 2005 with an exterior of inflated ETFE panels.
Colors change to represent the home team.
Hosted 2006 World Cup matches.
Located in the Fröttmaning area of Munich.

name: Signal Iduna Park
historyClues: Germany's largest stadium by capacity.
The Südtribüne is nicknamed the Yellow Wall.
Opened in 1974 for the World Cup.
Famous for intense atmosphere and tifo displays.

name: Parc des Princes
historyClues: Opened in 1972 in its current form with iconic concrete ribs.
Hosted numerous France national team matches.
Located in the 16th arrondissement.
Scene of PSG's domestic dominance in the 2010s and 2020s.

name: Stade Vélodrome
historyClues: Opened in 1937 and renovated for Euro 2016 with a sweeping roof.
Known for passionate support and intense derbies.
Hosts both football and rugby.
Located in the south of the city near the Prado.

name: San Siro
historyClues: Also known as Stadio Giuseppe Meazza.
Opened in 1926 and expanded multiple times.
Hosted World Cup and European finals.
Famous for its towering spiral ramps.

name: Allianz Stadium
historyClues: Opened in 2011 on the site of the old Delle Alpi.
Intimate design with seats close to the pitch.
Hosted UEFA club finals events.
Part of a larger commercial complex.
